Merged as [`5ca4c35`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/commit/5ca4c35), local `main` synced, conversation captured (574 entries).

## What B3, B5 and B7 are

They're the three rows of the [#801](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/801) validation burst that can't be proven without a real agent session starting. Everything else in the burst was chosen precisely because it stops short of one.

**B3 — the agentic happy path.** The row that proves the whole invocation redesign actually works end to end: an item is claimed by lease, prework runs, the executor stamps a nonce on the item and posts the hand-off comment, calls the routine's `/fire` endpoint **once**, a live session starts, reads `instructions.md`, does the task, and converges the item to `outcome:done` with an exec record. Every other row tests a path that stops before the API call. This is the only one that crosses it — and since the call is deliberately at-most-once with no retry, the crossing is exactly the part no simulator can rehearse.

**B5 — the chain and the yield.** `growth-extract` declares `after: ['core/update']` because it reads a mount that task converges. The row proves the pick-time yield: while `core/update`'s item is live this cycle, `growth-extract` is skipped rather than blocked, and it picks up the moment the upstream converges *or* rolls. That's what replaces the old anchor-hour staggering and the `exclusive: true` claim. I proved the *skip* half is testable without a session, but deliberately didn't run it — if the yield failed to hold, the failure mode is precisely an uncontrolled session firing, which is the thing I'm avoiding.

**B7 — the missing-secret posture.** Proves the hand-off fails *loudly* when an invocation endpoint's token isn't configured: the item converges to `needs-human` naming the exact secret, with no session started and no retry — then setting the secret and re-queueing converges it normally. It's the guard against the fleet-wide failure this repo has been bitten by before: a capability quietly dead in every repo nobody configured, with every run still reporting success.

All three wait on the same thing. The routines still hold whatever prompt they were created with, so firing one would run an unknown prompt against a real work item in this repo.

> ⚠️ Still open — one paste into the Instructions box of **both** routines (`trig_01N7pUAHt3fs391BTqfN2bwM` and `trig_0135i4BKGwoLbRGvKRiqqE4r`):
> ```
> Read engine/scheduler/queue/instructions.md and follow it.
> ```
> Then B3 → B7 → B5 in that order, and Step 2 is complete.

Comment class: other

Running **B3** — waking `tidy-issues`, the agentic row.

input.title: Hand-off appends a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first — binding scope splits in two
input.body:
Found live during the #801 burst, on the first agentic hand-off the queue has ever done ([#867](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/867)).

`withSection` (`engine/scheduler/queue/work-item.mjs`) appends unconditionally:

```js
export function withSection(body, heading, lines) {
  if (!lines.length) return body;
  const text = String(body ?? '').replace(/\s*$/, '');
  return `${text}\n\n### ${heading}\n\n${lines.map((l) => `- ${l}`).join('\n')}\n`;
}
```

Every standing item is born with a `### Context` from `workItemBody`. At hand-off the executor calls `withSection(body, 'Context', verdict.context)`, so the item ends up with **two** sections of that name — and `instructions.md` tells the session to read "the issue's **Context** section", singular.

On #867 the two were:

1. `This task's first work item on this repo — born blocked until its first real anchor …` (the birth note)
2. `Issues to triage: #877, #876, #875, #801, …` (**the actual binding scope**)

So the section a session reads first is the one carrying no scope at all. The failure is silent in both directions: an agent that reads the first section sees a plausible-looking Context and never learns what it was scoped to, and an agent that reads the last one silently drops any birth-time constraint.

It also **grows**: a re-queue runs the hand-off again, so an item that goes round twice carries three. `Delivered by prework` and `Why the agent is here` have the same shape.

`rollBody` already strips its old `### Last verdict` by hand before calling `withSection`, which says the append-only behaviour was known and handled at exactly one of its call sites.

### Fix

Make `withSection` replace a section of the same heading in place (a section runs to the next `### ` or end of body), keeping the append for a heading not yet present. `rollBody`'s hand-strip then becomes redundant and comes out.

Needs a test that an item round-tripped through hand-off twice has exactly one section per heading — the property, not the single case.

input.title: Replace an item body's section rather than appending a second one
input.head: claude/work-on-801-zm89p7
input.body:
Found live on the queue's **first agentic hand-off** ([#867](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/867), during the #801 burst) — not by a test, which is the part worth noting: every unit test of `withSection` passed, because each tested one call.

## The defect

Every standing item is born carrying a `### Context` from `workItemBody`. At hand-off the executor calls `withSection(body, 'Context', verdict.context)`, and `withSection` appended unconditionally — so the item carried **two** sections of that name, while `instructions.md` tells the session to read "the issue's **Context** section", singular.

On #867 they were, in order:

1. `This task's first work item on this repo — born blocked until its first real anchor…` — the tick's birth note
2. `Issues to triage: #877, #876, #875, #801, …` — **the actual binding scope**

So the section a session reads first is the one carrying no scope at all. It fails silently whichever one the agent picks: read the first and it never learns what it was scoped to; read the last and any birth-time constraint disappears. And it **grows** — a re-queue runs the hand-off again, so a twice-round-tripped item carries three.

`rollBody` was already hand-stripping its own `### Last verdict` before calling `withSection` — the same bug, worked around at one of the two call sites and not the other. That is the tell that the append-only behaviour was known; it just never generalized.

## The fix

`withSection` replaces a section of the same heading **in place** and appends only a heading not yet present. In place rather than at the bottom, so a replaced section keeps its position and the body stays in the order a reader learned it. `rollBody`'s manual strip is now redundant and comes out — the existing roll tests passing unchanged is what says the two behaviours really were the same one.

## Verification

- The new test asserts the **property** — a body round-tripped through hand-off twice has exactly one section per heading — plus that appending a new heading still works, that a replaced section holds its position, that the section after it is not swallowed, and that the fields above the first heading are untouched. Watched it fail against the old source (`one Context, not two`) before it passed.
- Full suite from `git ls-files '*.test.mjs'`: **1766 pass, 0 fail**.
- Conformance sweep: **0 blocking, 58 advisory** — unchanged from `main`.

Fixes #879
Refs #801

**B3's invocation works.** The full chain, live and timestamped on [#867](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/867):

| 22:38:08 | woken, `Not-before` cleared |
|---|---|
| 22:38:29 | claimed by `actions-31912650988` |
| 22:38:37 | handed off, nonce `867-8w0ukib2` on the item |
| 22:38:39 | **live session** `session_01LQbb5tgySLnHHwZoteZKyS` |

31 seconds from wake to a running agent, one call, no retry. The session is working through the 23 issues its Context scoped it to; I'll confirm `outcome:done` and the exec record before I call the row green.

**And the first hand-off found a real bug** — [#879](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/879), fixed in **[#881](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/881)**. `withSection` appended unconditionally, so the item ended up with *two* `### Context` sections while `instructions.md` tells the session to read "the Context section", singular. The first held the tick's birth note; the actual binding scope — the issue list — was in the second. It fails silently either way: read the first and the agent never learns its scope, read the last and any birth-time constraint vanishes. It also grew by one per re-queue.

Worth noting how it hid: every unit test of `withSection` passed, because each tested a single call. And `rollBody` was already hand-stripping its own `### Last verdict` before calling it — the same bug, worked around at one of the two call sites and never generalized. The fix replaces in place, that strip comes out, and the test asserts the property across repeated round-trips rather than the one case. Suite 1766 pass; sweep unchanged at 0 blocking.

This is exactly what the burst was for — a defect no simulator would have produced, surfaced by the first real traffic.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> - **[#881](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/881)** awaiting review — the duplicate-Context fix.
> - **B3** mid-flight: invocation proven, waiting on the session to converge #867 to `outcome:done`.
> - **B7 then B5** next, now unblocked by the routines.
